page.layout: One printed page: running head at top with page number 152 at left; a caption line under the title; a large woodcut of a shark (carcharias) occupying the centre; below the woodcut one block of text in full lines (German, Latin and English notes), with a catchword-like word "GLOSSO" at the lower right.

main_text.head: Hæc pictura Carchariæ Canis ad sceleton olim nobis facta est.
main_text.p: GER'M. Carcharias & Lamia siue unus, siue duo sunt pisces, propter generis tamen naturæ & cognationem uno nomine à Germanis appellari potest, ein Hrafsenfisch: ein Frass ed. r Flesshund, à ueracitate, uel à magnitudine ein Vdhund/ein grosser Hundsfisch/ein Malbuno. Belenius apud Norvegos Perkfisch uocari scribit, quasi montanum piscem.
ANGLI nimium communi ad Canes & Galeos nomine Dogg fishe nuncupant.

page.notes: The woodcut shows a shark (Carcharias) with spiny dorsal fins and a long tail; no text inside it. Several words of the German note are set in black letter and are approximate: "Hrafsenfisch" and "Vdhund", "ein Malbuno", "Belenius" and "Perkfisch" are doubtful. "GLOSSO" at lower right is a running catchword or signature mark and is not transcribed as text. The English word "Dogg" is partly obscured.
